hook.line: Every good story has a moment where you lean in and say "you won't believe this". Don Hernando does it every morning at the corner table.
hook.es: No te imaginas lo que me pasó ayer.
hook.en: You can't imagine what happened to me yesterday.

examples.es: No te imaginas lo que me pasó ayer.
examples.en: You can't imagine what happened to me yesterday.

examples.es: No te imaginas lo que me encontré al llegar.
examples.en: You can't imagine what I found when I got there.

examples.es: No sabes lo mal que la pasamos.
examples.en: You've no idea what a bad time we had.

examples.es: No te puedes ni imaginar lo rico que estaba el pan.
examples.en: You can't even imagine how good the bread was.

examples.es: No se imagina lo que dijo Simón, don Hernando.
examples.en: You can't imagine what Simón said, Don Hernando.

examples.es: No saben lo cansado que estoy.
examples.en: You all have no idea how tired I am.

rule:
This is the hook before the juicy part. Two shapes:

*No te imaginas lo que* plus a verb: what happened, what I found, what he said.

*No sabes lo* plus an adjective or adverb plus *que*: how tired, how badly, how good.

Swap *te* for *se* with *usted*, and use *saben* for *ustedes*. English says "you won't believe" or "you've no idea how". Spanish uses these two frames for both.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an attention-getter: a phrase that opens the complication of an anecdote.

readAndPick.es: No te imaginas lo que me pasó ayer.
options: You can't imagine what happened to me yesterday.
You can't imagine what happened to him yesterday.
I can't imagine what happened to you yesterday.

readAndPick.es: No sabes lo mal que la pasamos.
options: You've no idea what a bad time we're having.
You've no idea what a bad time we had.
You've no idea what a bad time they had.

readAndPick.es: No se imagina lo que dijo Simón, don Hernando.
options: I can't imagine what Simón said, Don Hernando.
You can't imagine what Simón said, Don Hernando.
You can't imagine what Simón is saying, Don Hernando.

readAndPick.es: No te puedes ni imaginar lo rico que estaba el pan.
options: You can't even imagine how good the bread was.
You can't even imagine how good the bread is.
I can't even imagine how good the bread was.

readAndPick.es: No saben lo cansado que estoy.
options: You all have no idea how tired I am.

options: You can't imagine what I found when I left.

You can't imagine what you found when you got there.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No te imaginas ___ me pasó ayer.* (*lo que* or *qué*) You can't imagine what happened to me yesterday.
yourTurn.answer: No te imaginas lo que me pasó ayer.
yourTurn.why: The hook uses *lo que*, then the story verb follows.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No sabes ___ mal que la pasamos.* (*lo* or *el*) You've no idea what a bad time we had.
yourTurn.answer: No sabes lo mal que la pasamos.
yourTurn.why: With an adjective or adverb the frame is *lo* plus the word plus *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: You can't imagine what I found when I got there.
yourTurn.answer: No te imaginas lo que me encontré al llegar.
yourTurn.why: *Al llegar* means when I got there, and *me encontré* says what I found.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: You've no idea how tired I am (a man speaking).
yourTurn.answer: No sabes lo cansado que estoy.
yourTurn.why: *Lo cansado que estoy* is the how-tired part; a man says *cansado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: You can't even imagine how good the bread was.
yourTurn.answer: No te puedes ni imaginar lo rico que estaba el pan.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it polite, to Don Hernando: *No te imaginas lo que me pasó ayer.*
yourTurn.answer: No se imagina lo que me pasó ayer.
accept: No se imagina lo que me pasó ayer, don Hernando.
yourTurn.why: With *usted* the pronoun *te* becomes *se* and the verb ends in *-a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it for several people (you all): *No sabes lo cansado que estoy.*
yourTurn.answer: No saben lo cansado que estoy.

pitfalls.right: No sabes lo cansado que estoy.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "how tired", but Spanish swaps *cómo* for *lo* and adds *que*: *lo cansado que*.

pitfalls.wrong: No te imagina lo que me pasó, don Hernando.
pitfalls.right: No se imagina lo que me pasó, don Hernando.
pitfalls.why: With *usted*, the pronoun changes too: *se imagina*, not *te imagina*.

pitfalls.wrong: No te imaginas lo que pasó me.
pitfalls.right: No te imaginas lo que me pasó.
pitfalls.why: The *me* goes before the verb: *me pasó*.

personal: Think of a story you have told this week. Open it with a hook: *No te imaginas lo que…*
